Baldur's Gate 3 · Script Extender mods · Patch 8

BG3 Mods Handbook

Two mods that run next to each other. Build Advisor tells you what to pick when you create or level a character. Loot Advisor shows which items suit that character's build and where to find them.

Build Advisor

Marks the strongest community build's choices in character creation, Withers' respec and every level-up.

Hotkey

For
every player, any character
State
working new version: not yet checked in game

Rainbow frames, rainbow map markers and an item list for the selected origin character, plus a live Sets page in your browser.

Hotkey

For
the 7 origin characters
State

Both need Baldur's Gate 3 Script Extender. BG3 Mod Manager can install it. The marks inside the game's own interface need Script Extender v33 or newer: Build Advisor's stars and outlines in the menus, Loot Advisor's item frames, tooltip lines and map painting. Everything else works on v32 (tested). Until v33 is a normal release, get it from the Devel channel: create a file ScriptExtenderUpdaterConfig.json in the game's bin folder containing {"UpdateChannel": "Devel"}, then start the game once. Delete that file to go back to normal releases. Each mod works on its own; Loot Advisor reads Build Advisor's build choice when both are installed.

Build Advisor

Build Advisor shows the strongest community build for your character and marks the right choices while you make them. It knows 22 builds, from Patch 8 community rankings and from damage and defence models made for the origin companions, and suggests two or three for each origin character.

It is for players who want a strong character without reading a build guide on a second screen, and for anyone respeccing a companion with Withers. It only reads the game and changes the text of the game's own menus while they are open. It never changes your character or your save.

New version, not yet checked in the game. The 22-build version marks every choice: stars on every named choice, rainbow outlines on tiles and spell icons, targets on level-up ability rows. It passes all offline checks, including every menu label compared with the game's own text. The in-game check comes next; until then, parts marked not yet checked in game may still change.

Requirements and install

NeedsScript Extender v33+
for the stars in the menus; the window works on v32
Game languageEnglish for the in-menu stars
the window works in any language
Save safetyNothing is written to saves
safe to add or remove at any time
  1. Install Script Extender (BG3 Mod Manager offers it). The stars and outlines need v33 or newer. Until v33 is a normal release, get it from the Devel channel: create a file ScriptExtenderUpdaterConfig.json in the game's bin folder containing {"UpdateChannel": "Devel"}, then start the game once. Delete that file to go back to normal releases.
  2. Import BuildAdvisor.pak with BG3 Mod Manager and enable it, then export the load order. Or copy the pak to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Larian Studios\Baldur's Gate 3\Mods\ and enable it in the game's mod manager.
  3. Start the game. If a Mod Verification dialog lists Build Advisor, tick it and choose Start Game. The Script Extender console prints [Build Advisor] loaded.

Uninstall: disable it in the mod manager or delete the pak. Your settings stay in BuildAdvisor_settings.json in the Script Extender folder; delete that file too if you want a clean slate.

Using it

Build Advisor works in four places. It finds out where you are by itself.

WhereWhat you seeWindow
New game character creationCustom Tav, the Dark Urge and origin characters. Every choice of the build is marked: race, class, subclass, background, deity, skills, cantrips and spells, and the point-buy rows. The window lists race, background, point buy and skills.Opens by itself
Withers' respecThe same as character creation, then every level-up that follows.Opens by itself
Level-upThe class to take this level, plus the subclass, feat, spells, manoeuvres or invocations to pick. The feat's own choices and the ability rows of an Ability Improvement are marked too.Opens by itself
Party view (normal play)Press F7 at any time: it shows the next level-up for the character you have selected.Hotkey only

Marks inside the game's own menus not yet checked in game

Every choice the build wants on the current screen is marked, in character creation, Withers' respec and every level-up. There are three kinds of mark.

  • A star in front of a name. Every choice that has a name in the menu gets a * prefix, which the game's font draws as a small star: race and subrace, class, subclass, background, deity (Clerics), skills and expertise, feats and the feat's own choices (for example * Resilient: Constitution), fighting styles, manoeuvres, invocations, metamagic, pact boons, draconic ancestry, favoured enemy and natural explorer, and the skill or cantrip a race lets you choose. Only the text changes; the menu works as before.
  • A rainbow outline on square picks. Tiles (race, subrace, class, subclass, background, deity) and spell and cantrip icons get the rainbow frame Loot Advisor uses for items, sized to the tile. Tiles keep the star on their name too. Spell and cantrip icons have no name in the grid, so they get the outline only. This covers new spells, prepared spells, spells a feat grants, and both sides of a spell swap.
  • Targets on ability rows, no star. Point buy shows the score to aim for: Strength (17, +2) means 17 is the final score and +2 is where your racial bonus goes; rows without a bonus read Dexterity (10). When the text would run under the row's minus button, the row uses the game's short name: CON (16, +1). At level-up, the ability rows of an Ability Improvement or a half feat show the same kind of target, for example Dexterity (19, +2): the score after the raise, and the raise. Rows the build does not raise are left alone.
  • * Change appears on the skill button when your current proficiencies are missing one of the build's skills. Open the picker; the build's skills are starred there.

When you leave the screen, pick another build, or untick Highlight in game menus, every star, outline and target disappears and the menu looks as before.

Stars on race, class and subclass names, the point-buy targets and the skill picker were confirmed in the game earlier. The other marks are new and are checked in the game next.

The advisor window

In character creation, respec and level-up the window sits right of the game's selection panel, with the same top and bottom as that panel, and stops short of the summary panel on the right. Outside these screens it opens between where the two panels would be. Move or resize it like any Script Extender window: once you do, it stays where you put it until you quit the game. F7 shows or hides it. It closes by itself when character creation, respec or level-up ends.

PartWhat it means
Build drop-downThe builds that fit this character. The first one is marked [Recommended]; the tier (S+, S, A) follows each name. Your pick is remembered for each character.
Show all buildsLists all 22 builds, not only the ones that fit.
Highlight in game menusTurns the stars and point-buy targets on or off. The window still works without them.
Auto-openOpens the window by itself in creation, respec and level-up.
Screen: characterThe screen (New character, Respec, Level up to N, Party) followed by the name, origin, race and current classes with subclass and level.
Build headerThe build name, then Tier – role, then one grey line on why it was suggested (best for this origin, starts as your class, uses your class, or matches your classes) with the origin's advice.
Do this nowWhat to pick on this screen. In creation and respec: race (best first and the alternatives; an origin's locked race in one short line), class with its choices, background, abilities with the +2 / +1 split, skills and, for clerics, the deity. In level-up: "Level N: class" and its choices. In the party view this heading reads Next level-up.
Your choicesOne green line names what already matches the plan (race, class, abilities). Each choice to change gets its own row with what to pick instead: red for race or class, amber for an ability score or class levels that differ from the plan (keep following the plan, or respec with Withers for 100 gold).
About this buildFolded: why the build is strong, the race reasons, the build's tips and a reminder about Withers.
Full level 1–12 planFolded table: level, class, choices. The current level is gold, past levels are grey.
Gear set 1–3With Loot Advisor installed: a spoiler note, then three folded sections, Loot Advisor's sets 1 to 3 for the selected build. Each holds one list per act (slot: item); "you have it" marks an item the party owns, "only if you already have it" an item that can no longer be found in that act. A grey line below points to Loot Advisor's F6 list and Sets page for where to find them. Without Loot Advisor, or for a build it has no sets for, only that line shows. The sets are read from Loot Advisor while the game runs; Build Advisor ships no item data.

Colours: green already matches, red or amber change this, gold headings and the current level, grey notes and past levels.

How it works

Finding the screen. Twice a second the mod looks at what the game is doing: a level-up in progress, a Withers respec, a new character being created, or, if none of those, the party member you control. From that it reads the name, origin, race, classes with subclasses and levels, the class being taken, and the ability scores (point-buy values in creation, final scores otherwise).

Ranking the builds. Builds are listed in this order, without repeats: the origin's own list (two or three builds; the Dark Urge has one too); builds that start as the class you picked; builds that use that class; builds that contain every class you already have; and with Show all builds, the rest by tier. The first entry is recommended unless you picked another one for this character.

Working out this step. Each build has a level-by-level plan (class taken at each character level, the picks, and the exact menu labels to star). The mod compares that plan with the character:

  • race: best pick, good alternative, or change (origin races are locked and always pass);
  • class this level: the class you are taking against the plan's class for this level;
  • class split so far: a warning when your levels per class differ from the plan;
  • abilities: in creation, each point-buy value against the plan (with the +2 / +1 racial bonus); later, each final score against the plan's minimum.

Marking the menus. Once a second, while a creation, respec or level-up screen is open, the mod walks the game's menu and marks every entry whose name is exactly one of this step's picks, written the way the game writes it. Matching is exact, so "Shield" never stars "Shield of Faith" and the cantrip "Light" never stars the Light Domain tile. Tiles and spell icons get the rainbow outline, point-buy and ability-improvement rows get their target, and the skill button gets * Change when skills are missing. Every menu label in the 22 builds was checked against the game's own text, and each pick against what the game offers at that class level. A walk took about 6 ms before the outlines were added; the new time is measured in the in-game check.

Settings

The three checkboxes and the build picker in the window are saved automatically. A few more options live in BuildAdvisor_settings.json in the Script Extender folder (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Larian Studios\Baldur's Gate 3\Script Extender\).

SettingDefaultMeaning
HotkeyF7Window key. F9 (photo mode) and F10 (hide interface) are game keys; an old F9 or F10 setting is moved to F7.
AutoOpentrueOpen in creation, respec and level-up.
HighlighttrueStars and point-buy targets in the game menus.
ShowAllfalseList every build.
FontScale0.75Text size of Script Extender windows (applies to all of them).
ChoicesemptyYour build pick per character. Loot Advisor reads it too.
UnsafeUiOnOldSEfalsetrue draws the stars and outlines on Script Extender older than v33 anyway. Older versions change the menus while the game draws them, which can crash the game; use v33 instead.

Console commands (Script Extender console): !ba_toggle opens or closes the window, !ba_hotkey F8 changes the key, !ba_dump prints what the mod detects (useful when something does not show).

Known limitations

  • The in-menu stars match English labels. In other game languages only the window helps.
  • Text rows (skills, feats, manoeuvres, invocations…) get a star only; a script cannot recolour the game's menu text. Tiles and spell icons get the rainbow outline.
  • The "You need a guardian" screen is treated like your own character creation.
  • Confirmed in the running game: character creation, origins, star marks on race, class and subclass, point-buy targets, the skill picker and auto-hide. Not yet checked in the game: the new marks (background, deity, feat choices, tile and spell outlines, level-up ability targets) and the 22-build lists in creation, Withers' respec and level-up.
  • Only the mouse-and-keyboard interface is supported; controller menus are laid out differently and are untested.
  • Builds are fixed. They reflect Patch 8 rankings and do not adapt to your gear or party.
  • If a game patch changes a menu, the affected part fails quietly. Untick Highlight in game menus if a menu looks wrong.

FAQ

Nothing opens when I press F7.

Check that Script Extender loaded (its console prints a line for each mod) and that Build Advisor is enabled. If you changed the key, the console line "[Build Advisor] loaded - press … to toggle" names it.

Can I follow a different build than the recommended one?

Yes. Pick it in the Build drop-down. The choice is saved per character and the stars follow it from then on.

My companion's levels don't match the plan.

The window warns you and keeps showing the plan's next step. Respec at Withers in camp (100 gold) to start clean; the mod guides the respec and every level-up after it.

Does it work for the Dark Urge or a custom Tav?

Yes. The Dark Urge gets a fixed list (the Throw-Thief first, the Throwzerker second), then builds for the class you pick. A custom Tav gets builds that start as, or use, the class you pick.

Will it break my save if I remove it?

No. It only reads the game and changes menu text while the menu is open.

For the developer source files and test notes
Main source files (client side only)
  • Shared/Builds.lua – the 22 builds and the origin → build lists (BA.Origins); each level's hl list holds the exact English menu labels to mark, plus bg, deity, raceHl, swap and asi for background, deity, race choices, spell swaps and ability raises.
  • Client/Detect.lua – reads creation / respec / level-up / party state.
  • Client/Advisor.lua – ranks builds, checks choices, builds the highlight list.
  • Client/Highlighter.lua – walks the game menu tree: exact label matching, named choice rows, tile and spell outlines, ability-row targets, a restore registry.
  • GUI/ – Build Advisor's own rainbow outline textures and a hidden resource page (brushes BA.TileRing, BA.IconRing, BA.Clear), so outlines work without Loot Advisor.
  • Client/Window.lua – the IMGUI window. Client/Main.lua – tick loop, hotkey, settings, console commands.
Debugging

"Debug": true in the settings file writes a debug text file with the skill-box search and a one-off dump of the menu tree on the point-buy screen; !ba_dump also prints the last menu pass time. Offline: tools/check_hl.py checks every label against the game's text and every pick against the class level (22 builds, 938 labels, 0 unknown); tools/mock_test.lua runs the mod against a mocked Script Extender. The in-game checklist is in HIGHLIGHT_STATUS.md.

Loot Advisor

Loot Advisor shows the rare items that best fit the character you have selected, and how to get them. Recommended items get a rainbow frame, their locations get rainbow diamonds on the map, and an item list (F6) explains each one. A Sets page in your browser shows full loadouts and follows your game live.

It covers the seven origin characters: Astarion, Gale, Karlach, Lae'zel, Shadowheart, Wyll and the Dark Urge. Advice follows that character's actual build, the current act, your story choices and what the party already owns. Items that need a theft, a kill or a story choice are included with a warning.

Spoiler warning: Loot Advisor names items, where they are and who carries them, and its notes reveal story outcomes (who can die, which side you take, endings).

Requirements and install

NeedsScript Extender v33+
for frames and map painting; the list and Sets page work on v32
OptionalBuild Advisor
your build pick there is used to break ties
Disk1.2 MB pak
+ about 18 MB for the Sets page, built on first load
  1. Install Script Extender. Item frames and map painting need v33 or newer. Until v33 is a normal release, get it from the Devel channel: create a file ScriptExtenderUpdaterConfig.json in the game's bin folder containing {"UpdateChannel": "Devel"}, then start the game once. Delete that file to go back to normal releases.
  2. Import LootAdvisor.pak with BG3 Mod Manager and enable it (or copy it to the game's Mods folder and enable it in the game's mod manager).
  3. Start the game and load a save. Tick Loot Advisor if the Mod Verification dialog lists it. The console prints [Loot Advisor] loaded - F6 toggles the item list.
  4. Select an origin character. Frames and map markers appear within about a second; press F6 for the list.
  5. For the Sets page, open %LOCALAPPDATA%\Larian Studios\Baldur's Gate 3\Script Extender\LootAdvisor\Sets.html in your browser and bookmark it (F6 > Open Sets page shows this path, ready to copy). The console prints a line when the page is ready (about 8 seconds after the first load, under a second later on).

Uninstall. Turn markers off first ("Enabled": false in the settings, see Settings), then save, then disable the mod. Shown map markers are part of the game's journal state and may be stored in a save made while they were visible. Removing the mod from such a save has not been tested yet. Tooltip texts and frames are never saved. To clean up fully, delete the LootAdvisor folder and LootAdvisor_settings.json in the Script Extender folder.

Signs in the game

Rainbow frame on items

A recommended item gets a rainbow "prism" frame instead of the game's rarity frame. It shows wherever the item appears: inventory and bags, equipment slots on the character sheet, the hotbar, opened containers, the camp chest, the inventory search view and your side of the trade window. A bag that holds a recommended item gets the frame too. When the item stops being recommended, the game's own frame comes back.

Framed: items you own, items with a map marker, set items, items in another area and items with no fixed spot. Not framed: items whose story path is closed, items better kept for another companion, and items shown only in the list (random loot, generic +1 / +2 gear), which get no frame and no tooltip row either.

Rainbow diamond on the map

Each item to fetch gets a marker on the minimap and the world map (M). It looks like the game's gold quest diamond, in rainbow colours. Hover it for its label:

Map label
Sword of Chaos
Helldusk Gloves
Elixir of Viciousness

The label shows the rainbow diamond and a plain list of the items you can get there, one per line, in the same cyan as the tooltip advice. When a marker covers several characters, each item is followed by the names it is for. Hovering the marker shows a Loot Advisor title with the rainbow diamond above that list.

Markers show the best and runner-up item per slot for the current act, for the character you have selected. Select someone else and the markers switch to that character. Once the party owns an item, its marker disappears; the frame stays.

Off-screen arrows

Markers for everyone. The map marks the items of everyone in your party, your camp and the companions who may still join (Halsin, Jaheira, Minsc and Minthara too, unless dead or gone for good), plus Tavs and hirelings. One marker per spot: hovering it lists each item with the names it is for. Choose whose items are marked in the F6 list: Everyone, The active party or The selected character.

When a marked item is outside the minimap, the game draws its own off-screen arrow at the minimap rim, recoloured in rainbow. Only the 5 best markers of the selected character get an arrow (best before runner-up, then in slot order), so the rim does not fill up; the markers of everyone else never get one. Items visible on the minimap show the diamond and no arrow. The world map does the same at its edges.

Entrance and region-exit markers

Many items lie inside places you cannot see from outside: vaults, cellars, the House of Hope, the Guildhall. For those, the marker goes on the entrance on the shortest way from where you stand: a door, ladder, hatch or portal. If the item is two areas deep, the marker sits on the first entrance on the way. Step inside and the marker moves to the next entrance, or to the item itself.

An item in another region (for example Wyrm's Crossing while you are in the Lower City) gets a marker on the way out of this region: a gate, lift or other region exit. Where no walking route leads there, the nearest waypoint is marked: fast travel from there. Several items behind the same entrance share one marker, and its label lists them all.

Advice in item tooltips

Hover a recommended item: under the game's description, one extra row appears, laid out like the tooltip's own rows. The rainbow diamond sits in the icon column at the size of the game's icons, and the text is cyan, a colour the game does not use in its descriptions. The row has at most two lines:

Tooltip row, examples
Best Gloves for Astarion
On your map · +1 attack rolls; grants Garrotte
Runner-up Armour for Karlach
Better on Lae'zel
Set Cloak for Gale
In another area · Community pick
LineWhat it says
1Best, Runner-up or Set, the slot, and the character it is for.
2-4The most important of: "Better on X"; "Path closed: …"; "Shared pick with X"; the item's warning (a theft, a kill, a story choice or a missable item) in a short form of up to three lines that keeps every name, act and cost; otherwise the status ("You have it", "On your map", "In another area", "No fixed spot (see F6)", "Only if you already have it") and a short reason.

The full reason, all warnings, the sets and how to get it are in the F6 list and on the Sets page. The row follows the selected character, is never stored in your save, and applies to every copy of the same item. Items shown only in the list get no row. It appears wherever the game shows an item tooltip: your bags, both sides of the trade window, pickpocketing, a corpse's loot and the camp chest. For the Dark Urge it uses your character's own name.

The item list (F6)

Press F6 to show or hide the list. It covers everything, including items that have no marker. Directions update every second while it is open.

Header

Line 1 (gold): character, act and the build Loot Advisor matched to the character. Line 2 (grey): the region, the number of items and markers, and the hotkey. Hover line 2 for why that build was picked (for example "closest to your class levels" or "closest to your classes; Build Advisor's order"). For a character on none of the builds an amber line 3 names the closest build, how alike it is and whose sets it uses, for example "Closest build: Path of Giants Barbarian 12 (64% alike; Karlach's sets)".

Open Sets page sits above the header. The game cannot open a browser or write to the clipboard, so the button shows the page's path in a field instead: click the field (it selects the whole path), press Ctrl+C, then paste it into your browser's address bar, or press Win+R, Ctrl+V, Enter. The same button hides the path again.

Made for Build Advisor's builds. Loot Advisor's sets are made for the builds of Build Advisor. Any other character (Halsin, Jaheira, Minsc, Minthara, a custom Tav, a hireling, or an origin respecced into a class mix none of its builds has) gets the closest Build Advisor build: most alike in class levels, then subclass, main ability, caster type and weapon style; equal ones go to the build you picked in Build Advisor, then to the one with fewer classes. The header names that build and how alike it is, and the item tooltips read "Best <slot> for <name> (closest build)".

Legend

"Next – nearest items you can get now"

Up to six marked items, nearest first: item, slot, direction and distance from the selected character (compass point and metres, north = up on the minimap), and where the marker leads ("Enter Murder Tribunal", "Way out to Wyrm's Crossing", "On your map: Sorcerous Sundries"). Hover "where" for the full how-to text.

Story paths and the party

Story-path gating. Loot Advisor reads your game's story state: Shadowheart's Shar or Selûne path, whether the goblins raided the Grove or the tieflings were saved, Isobel's fate at Last Light, whether Mizora was freed, the Murder Tribunal, who is dead, and whether this is a Dark Urge campaign. An item behind a closed path is greyed with the reason, for example path closed: needs Shadowheart's Shar path or lost: Isobel's death (Last Light falls) happened. Dark Urge-only items read "Dark Urge campaign only" in other campaigns.

Items that cost a companion. An item whose price is losing one of the origin companions is left out completely, unless that has already happened in your game.

"Better on X". Some items are unique. Each unique item has one best owner, based on how much each build gets from it, decided among your active party (the up to four characters with you; companions waiting in camp don't count). Other characters see the item greyed as "Better on X", and their runner-up moves up. The item list, the tooltips, the map markers and the Sets page all decide it the same way.

Tie picks. When two party members fit a unique item exactly equally, both see "(shared)" in the Pick column and "Shared pick with …" in the tooltip until you decide: the F6 list shows the tie with a Give it to … button per character (the Sets page has the same buttons). The other one then moves to the next pick. Whoever already wears the item keeps it. Your pick is kept when the party changes; you are asked again only for a new tie.

Owned items count from the party's inventories and bags, members waiting in camp, and every camp chest. An item turns to "Owned" within about a second of picking it up.

The Sets page

A local web page that ships with the mod and shows complete loadouts ("synergy sets") for each origin character and act: about 240 sets in total. Open it in Chrome, Edge or Firefox while you play. It updates by itself; there is no folder to pick, no file to load and no extra program.

No game art ships with the mod. On your first load the mod builds the page's icons, fonts and item texts from your own game install, in your game's language. Loot Advisor's own advice text is in English.

Parts of the page

PartWhat it does
Act buttons I · II · IIISets are per act. Items of earlier acts appear only as "if you have it".
Live indicatorLive (green dot): connected, time of the last change, act, region, nearby area and selected character. Game not running (red dot): no update for 25 seconds; the page shows the last known state. Waiting for the game: nothing received yet.
My playthroughDark Urge playthrough, Grove fight, Shadowheart and the Nightsong, Isobel at Last Light, Theft and killing neutrals. Each reads "From your game: …"; choosing a value overrides it, and Use my game for everything drops the overrides. Hide earlier-act items I don't have removes items you can no longer get.
Character portraitsThe seven origin characters. The one selected in the game opens by itself, on the set of the build closest to the character's real classes.
Set listSets in order: main build, community builds, auto-picked sets. Chips: Main pick, Alternative 1–2, Option N; Community build or Auto-picked; "11/11 available" with your settings; coloured pills count story, crime, missable, earlier-act and party items.
Shopping listWhat to fetch: missable items first, then grouped along the act's route, earlier-act items last. Each row has a Have it tick, the slot, ◆ core for the item the set is built around, where to get it and coloured notes (Theft / kill, Missable, Tip, Party).
Equipment and sheetA paperdoll like the game's; hover an item for a game-style tooltip with Loot Advisor's notes on top. The character sheet (abilities, AC, HP, attacks, spell DC, resistances, granted actions) is computed at the character's real level; hover any number for its formula. Level 12 switches to the end-game numbers.

Compare two setsPick A and B; differing slots get a dashed outline, and a delta column shows ▲ better / ▼ worse, plus counts of story locks, thefts and missables.

Live sync

While the game runs, the mod writes a small state file at most every 2 seconds when something changes (items picked up or moved, level-ups, party changes, story flags, deaths, a new save loaded, the selected character, a new area) and every 10 seconds anyway. The page re-reads it every 3 seconds and at once when you switch to its tab. A pickup in the game shows on the page within about 3–5 seconds.

  • Have it ticks fill from the party, camp members and camp chests ("In your game", with who holds it on hover). Manual ticks still work for other items.
  • Contested items follow your active party: if someone in the party gets more from an item, this character's slot uses the alternative; an exact tie is a tie pick: the game's pick (or whoever wears it) wins, otherwise pick on the page with the Give it to … buttons.
  • The character sheet uses the character's real level.

How items are picked

Before release: scoring every item

Every weapon, armour piece and accessory in the game was read from the game files with its stats, effects and where it comes from. Each item is then scored for each build of each origin character, per act:

  • Usable at all? Armour and weapons the build is not proficient with are dropped, unless the item grants the proficiency. Build rules apply (no shield for a Monk, no heavy armour for a Bladesinger).
  • Build fit. Rarity; for weapons, how well the weapon matches the build's attack style plus its damage and enchantment; for armour, the AC the build really gets with its Dexterity (or its Unarmoured Defence); then every effect of the item, weighted by what the build needs. Effects with a condition the build doesn't arrange count less. Race-only effects count only for that race. Known Patch 8 bugs are scored as the game behaves, and the "why" text says so.
  • Community consensus. Items named in popular build guides for that build get extra points (best pick, runner-up, part of a set), up to a cap.
  • Act. An item counts from the first act it can reliably be obtained in (world, container, reward, trader, NPC) to the last act it can still be obtained in.

That gives a best and runner-up per slot per act, and the synergy sets: sets taken from community builds, plus an auto-picked "best overall" loadout and theme sets that reach at least 85% of its score. Every set is legal: two-handed weapons keep the off hand empty, dual wielding needs light weapons, and no set mixes items whose story paths exclude each other. Items with a condition get a fallback; unique items get a party owner and an alternative for everyone else.

In the game: matching your character

Build matching. The selected character's live classes, subclasses and levels are compared with each of that character's builds. A class the build uses scores its levels (up to the build's own); a matching subclass adds a bonus; levels in classes the build doesn't use count against it. The highest score wins. On a tie, Build Advisor's pick for that character wins, then Build Advisor's build order. With no class in common, the build is chosen by the character's highest ability.

Recommending. For the matched build and the current act (taken from the region you are in), each slot's best and runner-up are checked against your game: owned, path closed, better on someone else, earlier act, random loot. If a pick is unusable, the next candidate moves up. Set slots follow the same rules, with these swaps:

  • in a Dark Urge campaign, a Dark Urge-only item that beats the set's pick replaces it;
  • an earlier-act item the party owns that is better replaces it;
  • otherwise the set's fallback is used.

Markers are shown for the best and runner-up of each slot that have a fixed spot in this region. Items in another area or region are routed to an entrance or exit (shortest way from the selected character, re-checked when you move into another area). Frames go on everything recommended that isn't random loot, closed, or better on someone else.

When it updates. The recommendation is recomputed when items move, a story flag is set, someone dies, the selection or a level changes, or you enter another area, and every 20 seconds otherwise. A recompute takes about 20–40 ms. Frames and marker colours are repainted twice a second (4–16 ms).

Settings and the dev toggle

Settings live in LootAdvisor_settings.json in the Script Extender folder. The mod re-reads the file every few seconds, so edits apply without a restart. Only keys you want to change need to be in it.

KeyDefaultMeaning
EnabledtrueMaster switch. false hides all markers, restores frames and tooltip texts.
HotkeyF6Key for the item list.
FramestrueRainbow frames on items.
MarkerstrueMap markers.
Tooltipstrue"Why" text in item tooltips.
Arrows5How many off-screen markers keep a rainbow arrow.
UnsafeUiOnOldSEfalsetrue draws frames, tooltip lines and map painting on Script Extender older than v33 anyway. Older versions change the interface while the game draws it, which can crash the game (seen in combat); use v33 instead.
MarkerFilter"all"Whose items get map markers: "all" (party, camp, companions who may still join), "party" or "selected". The F6 list sets it.
SpoilerNoticeSeenfalseSet to true by Got it, hide this under the spoiler warning in the F6 list; false shows the warning again.
Pagetruefalse stops writing the Sets page and its live state.
ActOverridenoneForce act 1, 2 or 3 instead of the one detected from your region.
NorthZ, EastX1Set to -1 to flip the list's compass if directions ever look mirrored.
DevfalseDeveloper mode, see below.

Dev toggle: !la_dev in the Script Extender console switches Dev on or off and saves it. With Dev on, the item list shows an extra grey line with the story state Loot Advisor read (paths, region, area), and test helpers become active that can spawn items and move characters. Those helpers are meant for test saves. Players should leave Dev off.

Known limitations

  • Scored builds are Build Advisor's builds for the origins. Halsin, Jaheira, Minsc, Minthara, hirelings, custom characters and respecced origins get the closest of those builds, named in the F6 header.
  • Frames and tooltips follow the selected character. Map markers cover everyone (see the filter in the F6 list).
  • Some items have no fixed spot (quest rewards, boss drops, forge results) and appear in the list only. A few traders are marked on the trader in person; the game draws those only when you are near them.
  • Areas are recognised from where things are placed in the level. Rarely, an interior is not recognised and the marker stays on the item itself, which then shows as an edge arrow.
  • "Fast travel" routes are checked offline only.
  • Map markers may be stored in a save made while they were shown; removing the mod from a save is not tested yet (see Uninstall).
  • Controller mode and the low-resolution interface are not tested.
  • Advice texts are English. Item names and game texts on the Sets page follow your game language.
  • The tooltip shows a shortened warning (up to three lines); the full text is in the F6 list and on the Sets page.
  • The list window uses * instead of the diamond, because its font has no diamond.
  • Item names in the in-game list are English; the Sets page uses your game language.
  • The Sets page: Chrome and Edge slow down tabs hidden for more than about 5 minutes (updates then arrive within a minute, and at once when you switch to the tab; Firefox keeps polling). Each page open needs 3–4 seconds to build its images. The area name is approximate ("near …"). In multiplayer only the host writes the page.

FAQ

I see no frames or markers.

Select a character and press F6: the header says which character and build Loot Advisor is using. Check that Enabled, Frames and Markers are not set to false.

Why is an item I want greyed out?

Hover its status. "Path closed" names the story choice, "Better on X" names the companion who gets more from it, "If you have it" means it is from an earlier act.

The marker is on a door, not on the item.

The item is inside that area. Go through the marked entrance; the marker moves on. "Way out marked" means the item is in another region.

Two characters both want the same unique item.

If one fits it better, the other sees "Better on X" and moves to the next pick. If they fit it equally, both see "shared pick" and you decide with the Give it to … buttons in the F6 list or on the Sets page; whoever wears it keeps it.

Does it spoil the story?

It names item locations, holders and the story choices that open or close them. Treat it as a guide with spoilers.

Can I trust the Sets page numbers?

They are computed from the game's own item and class rules; hover a number to see its formula. Some class features (Rage, Sneak Attack, smites, spells such as Shield) are not added.

The Sets page says "Game not running".

No update for 25 seconds: the game is closed, still loading, or Page is false. It catches up as soon as the game writes again.

For the developer source files and data flow
Server side (story state, recommendation, markers)
  • Server/State.lua – region and act, story paths from flags and dead NPCs, companions, Dark Urge campaign, owned items (party, bags, camp members, all camp chests), live marker positions.
  • Shared/Logic.lua – MatchBuild and Recommend: status per item, set swaps (ca, oa, fallbacks), markers and frames.
  • Shared/Zones.lua – zone lookup, shortest route over entrance links, WayOut for other regions.
  • Server/Main.lua – refresh loop, journal markers via ShowMapMarker, label texts, result to the client.
  • Server/PageSync.lua + Shared/ShipManifest.lua – writes the Sets page, game art and texts, and the live state script.
  • Server/Cheats.lua – Dev-only command file: spawn, tp, tpto, refresh.
Client side (selection and painting)
  • Client/Selected.lua – selected character, origin, live classes, Build Advisor pick and order.
  • Client/Paint.lua + Client/UiTree.lua – rainbow frames, marker icon and arrow textures, 5-arrow limit, restoring recycled game markers.
  • Client/Tooltip.lua – the advice row: swaps the tooltip's description strip for our template (Pages/LootAdvisorRes.xaml, LA.ItemAdviceTemplate) while a recommended item is hovered and puts the game's back afterwards; the diamond in front of our marker labels. One shared colour resource LA.AdviceBrush (#66FFD9) for both. Checked in game.
  • Client/Window.lua – the F6 list and the Sets page path field (Script Extender cannot open a URL or set the clipboard, so the player copies the path).
Generated data

Shared/LootData.lua (items, builds, sets, owners) and Shared/ModData.lua (marker spots, zones, entrances, region exits, story flags) are generated offline; the 337+ journal markers live under Story/Journal/Markers. The rainbow textures and the hidden resource widget are in GUI/.

Written from the mods' own code and test results, 10 October 2026. Baldur's Gate 3 is a game by Larian Studios; screenshots show the mods running in the game. Script Extender is a separate community project.
